title: A tree includes its earlier levels
hook: Count every node visited, not just the final layer.

doesNotKnow: Distinguish terminal-layer size from cumulative full-tree visits.

misconception: Last-level node count equals the total work of visiting a tree.
objective: Distinguish terminal-layer size from cumulative full-tree visits.

claims.text: Tree analysis requires counting all relevant nodes in the data structure.
Donald E. Knuth, The Art of Computer Programming, Volume 1: Fundamental Algorithms (1968)
The unary path contains {A}; the binary tree contains {B}. The final layer is only part of each total because earlier nodes remain.
Does it hold up? This is a full collision-free tree, not a search with incomplete branches or reused states.
claims.source: {"type":"source-access-hold","note":"No empirical effect or research verdict established. Only bounded arithmetic proposed."}

recall.question: A complete directory has a root, three folders and nine leaf folders. Visiting every node takes how many visits?
recall.why: 1+3+9=13; counting leaves alone omits earlier levels.
